We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to a phenyl ring (the sulfonyl phenyl) which is para-substituted with the unsaturated amide chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (aniline). So target has three key bonds: sulfonamide N-S, amide C-N, and the C=C double bond formed via Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid). So retrosynthesis steps: 1) disconnect amide: break C(=O)-N bond to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) disconnect C=C double bond: break to give aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid (or its derivative). 3) disconnect sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the p-tolyl amine). Actually sulfonamide formed from p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from the other phenyl sulfonyl chloride (maybe 4-sulfonyl chloride). But target sulfonamide is N attached to p-tolyl (methyl phenyl) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring. So retrosynthesis: break N-S to give p-toluidine (or its protected) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2). Then later sulfonyl chloride can be made from corresponding phenyl sulfonic acid (via chlorination). But we only need 3 steps, so we can have: Step1: amide formation (coupling) from α,β-unsaturated acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step2: Doebner modification to make α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid. Step3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2). However we need to incorporate the sulfonamide onto the same molecule that already contains the unsaturated amide chain attached to the phenyl ring. Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl, and the sulfonyl group attached to the phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide. So the sulfonamide formation step should connect p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) with the sulfonyl chloride derived from the phenyl bearing the unsaturated acid (after step2). So after step2 we have phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait step2 yields α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(C=CC(=O)O)cc2). To get sulfonyl chloride, we need to convert that phenyl to sulfonyl chloride (i.e., sulfonylation). But the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring, not the acid side chain. Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring (the same phenyl that also bears the unsaturated amide). So the phenyl ring has two substituents: sulfonyl group (SO2-) attached to N of p-tolyl, and the unsaturated amide chain attached via para position? Let's examine SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: Starting with Cc1ccc(... )cc1 is p-tolyl ring with substituent NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to p-tolyl. The sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl ring c2ccc(... )cc2 which has the unsaturated amide chain at para position relative to sulfonyl? Actually the SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc...), and that phenyl also has the unsaturated amide chain at para position (maybe). So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2). Then later we need to attach the unsaturated amide chain onto that aryl sulfonyl chloride (i.e., the phenyl ring already has the unsaturated amide chain). Actually the unsaturated amide chain is attached to the same phenyl ring; we can construct that phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide chain first (via Doebner and amide formation) to give the aryl carboxylic acid (or amide) attached to phenyl, then convert the phenyl to sulfonyl chloride (by sulfonation? but sulfonyl chloride is not derived from carboxylic acid). Might be easier: Step1: amide formation (C=O + aniline). Step2: Doebner modification to create α,β-unsaturated acid (or acid then amide). Step3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl (maybe via chlorosulfonation of phenyl). But we need only 3 steps; we can treat sulfonyl chloride as commercially available (or derived from phenyl sulfonic acid). So we can propose that the sulfonyl chloride is a building block.

Thus route: Target -> disconnect amide -> gives α,β-unsaturated acid (C=CC(=O)O attached to phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then disconnect C=C -> gives aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then disconnect sulfonamide -> gives p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2). However note that after step2 we have aldehyde attached to phenyl that will later be sulfonylated? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring, not the aldehyde. So the phenyl ring after step2 is the same as the sulfonyl chloride phenyl. So we need to have the phenyl ring bearing both aldehyde (for Doebner) and later sulfonyl chloride (for sulfonamide). But we cannot have both functional groups on same carbon; they are para to each other. So we need a phenyl with two substituents: aldehyde and sulfonyl chloride. That is possible: 4-formyl-phenyl sulfonyl chloride. So step2: Doebner modification on 4-formyl-phenyl sulfonyl chloride? But sulfonyl chloride may be incompatible with Doebner conditions. However for retrosynthesis we can assume it's okay or we can reorder: first sulfonyl chloride formation from phenyl with aldehyde, then Doebner. But we have only 3 steps; we can treat sulfonyl chloride as a building block that already has aldehyde (i.e., 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). So step3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and that sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide attached to phenyl bearing aldehyde. Step2: Doebner modification on that aldehyde phenyl sulfonyl chloride to give α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. Step1: amide coupling to give final product.

Thus we need templates for: amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Doebner modification (aryl aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). Sulfonamide formation (aryl sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide). We need to find template IDs for these reactions.

Search for sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_broken: ["sulfonic"]? Actually sulfonyl chloride to sulfonamide: break S-Cl bond, form S-N. So broken functional group: "sulfonic"? The list includes "sulfonic" maybe refers to sulfonyl chloride? The functional group list includes "sulfonic" and "sulfonamides". So we can search with broken "sulfonic" and formed "sulfonamides". Already attempted earlier with c1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 and got empty. Maybe need to specify "sulfonyl chlorides"? Not in list. Could be "sulfonic" is correct. But result empty maybe due to limited database. Could try search without specifying broken, just formed "sulfonamides".
